passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of two novel cognitive training programs on reaction time in adults aged 20–35. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group receiving no training, Treatment A (visual‑spatial drills), Treatment B (verbal memory tasks), or a combined group that performed both treatments in sequence. Over a 4‑week period, participants completed a computerized simple reaction time task at baseline, mid‑intervention, and post‑intervention. Mean reaction times (in milliseconds) and standard deviations were recorded at each assessment point. The table below summarizes the post‑intervention results for the four groups. The researchers hypothesized that the combined training would produce the greatest reduction in reaction time, reflecting synergistic effects of multimodal practice. Statistical analysis included one‑way ANOVA followed by post‑hoc Tukey tests to compare group means. Findings suggested a significant difference between the combined group and the control group, but not between the two single‑treatment groups. The study contributes to the literature on cognitive enhancement and informs future experimental designs in this domain.
stem: Which group had the lowest mean reaction time?
explanation: The combined group had a mean of 320 ms, the lowest among all groups.
trap: Some may incorrectly assume the control group had the lowest because it received no training.

stem: Which experimental design best tests whether the combined treatment is more effective than the single treatments?

options.A: Randomized controlled trial with separate groups

explanation: A randomized controlled trial with separate groups isolates the effect of each treatment and the combination, allowing direct comparison.
trap: A crossover design might seem appropriate but would confound the order of treatments.

stem: If the combined group mean is 320 ms with SD = 40 ms and n = 30, what is the 95% confidence interval for the mean?
trap: Understating the margin of error (options A and C, about +/-10 to 12 ms) instead of using t x SE = 2.045 x 7.30 = 14.9 ms.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a potential source of bias in this study?
explanation: Randomization reduces bias; it is not a source of bias itself.
trap: Some may think randomization introduces bias because it changes group composition.

stem: Which statement is supported by the post-intervention data in the table?

options.A: The Combined group mean reaction time was 30 ms lower than the Control group mean.
options.B: Treatment B had a lower mean reaction time than Treatment A.
options.C: The Control group had the smallest SD.
options.D: The mean reaction times of Treatment A and Treatment B differed by 20 ms.

explanation: Correct: 350 - 320 = 30 ms. Why the others are wrong: B) Treatment B (340 ms) was higher than Treatment A (330 ms). C) Control had the largest SD (45), not the smallest. D) 340 - 330 = 10 ms, not 20 ms.
trap: Misreading the table: choosing D (20 ms) for the Treatment A versus B gap, which is really 10 ms, or treating control as having the smallest SD when it has the largest.
